newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt sees 500 mln ATS costs from EMU.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt sees 500 mln ATS costs from EMU.

text.p: The introduction of Europe's single currency will cost Austria's Creditanstalt as much as half a billion schillings in one-off costs over a two- to three-year period, the bank said on Thursday.

Board member Roman Fojtl said the bank expected revenues to fall by a similar amount. "And that's not just once, but over a long period," he told a conference on the planned single currency organised by the Austrian industrialists' association.

"At the beginning, the euro will mean nothing but costs," Fojtl said, adding that only after a "very long" warm-up period could banks expect to gain from Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), now scheduled to go into effect by 1999.

Austrian banks have calculated the overall cost of introducing the euro at about eight billion schillings, and revenue losses at 3.5 billion for the industry as a whole. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
